measuredRatioApprox: 2.22:1 (border #767676 vs card #a9b7c6) — NOT vs page white (4.54:1)
rationale: The button border must be judged against the card it sits on (#a9b7c6 = 2.22:1), not the page background (#ffffff = 4.54:1). Against the actual adjacent surface it fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: contrast is measured against 'adjacent color(s)'; G174/G207 require 3:1 with the surrounding color the component is placed on.

measuredRatioApprox: 2.17:1 (outline #808080 vs panel #c0c0c0) — vs white would be 3.95:1
rationale: The input boundary is 2.17:1 against the panel it sits on; the page-background comparison (3.95:1) is the wrong surface. Fails against the actual adjacent color.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; G174 (3:1 between control boundary and adjacent colors).

rationale: The toggle's track outline and knob are 2.06:1 against the card surface, below 3:1; against page white they would appear to pass (4.54:1).
The comparison surface is the inner card the button sits on (#b8c4d8 = 2.58:1), not the outer white card. Against the true adjacent surface it fails.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: adjacent color is the immediate surrounding surface; G174.

measuredRatioApprox: 2.73:1 (wedge #6f93b8 vs neighbor #5e84ab) — each is >3:1 vs white
rationale: Each wedge contrasts well with the white page, but the boundary that matters is wedge-vs-neighbor (2.73:1). The adjacent surface is the other wedge, and that pair fails.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: 3:1 is required against 'adjacent colors', i.e. the neighboring graphical part; G207; F78.

rationale: The focus ring overlaps the selected row's background (#c0c0c0); the ring must be compared to that adjacent surface (2.17:1), not the white page.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 (focus indicators are graphical objects required to operate); the adjacent color is the surface the ring sits against; G195.

rationale: The plus glyph that conveys 'add' is on the gray button face; judged against that surface it is ~1.4:1, far below 3:1. The page background is irrelevant here.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; the comparison surface is the immediate adjacent color (button face); G207.

rationale: The status dot on the shaded row is 2.22:1 against that row; the dot is a meaning-bearing graphic and must contrast with its actual adjacent surface, which it does not.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; G207; the adjacent color is the row shade, not the white page.

rationale: The CTA border is 2.31:1 against the brand banner it sits on; a page-background measurement (5.1:1) would wrongly pass it.
The boundary that communicates progress is fill-vs-track (1.69:1). The track is the adjacent surface; that pair fails 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; G207; the adjacent color is the track, not the page.

rationale: The selected/unselected segments are distinguished only by their adjacent fill boundary (~1.2:1). The comparison surface is the neighbor segment, and it fails.
The callout border must be compared to the dark scrim it sits on (~1.4:1), not the white page; it fails 3:1 against the actual adjacent surface.
Even judged against the actual card surface, the border exceeds 3:1.
The outline contrasts well with the cream panel it sits on.

measuredRatioApprox: 7.54:1 (border #bdbdbd vs dark card #2b2b2b) — only 1.88:1 vs white
rationale: A naive page-background check (1.88:1 vs white) would wrongly fail this, but the border sits on a dark card and is 7.54:1 against the actual adjacent surface. No barrier.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: the comparison is against the adjacent color (dark card), not the page; G174.

rationale: The ring overlaps a dark row and is 6.80:1 against that adjacent surface; passes 3:1.
Adjacent wedges contrast above 3:1 with each other.
Fill contrasts strongly with the unfilled track.

measuredRatioApprox: indeterminate (border crosses a gradient card; adjacent color varies)
rationale: The adjacent surface is a gradient that ranges from light to dark, so a single deterministic contrast value is undefined; the runner must abstain rather than emit a verdict.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: contrast is against 'adjacent colors'; where the adjacent surface varies continuously, deterministic single-value evaluation is not sound.

rationale: The button border sits over a varying photographic-style backdrop; there is no single adjacent color to compare, so the runner must abstain.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11; adjacent-color comparison is undefined over a varying image surface.

rationale: Here the adjacent surface genuinely is the white page, and the border passes against it.
Judged against the correct inner-card surface, the border passes.

measuredRatioApprox: >=7:1 (border #595959 vs the white page it actually borders)
rationale: Although a card is nearby, the button's boundary actually meets the white page; against that true adjacent surface it passes.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: compare to the adjacent color the boundary actually meets; G174.

rationale: The plus glyph contrasts strongly with the button face it sits on.
